explanation_template: Dairy products can reduce the absorption of some antibiotics, especially medicines such as tetracyclines or fluoroquinolones. When the medicine is taken close to milk, yogurt, cheese, or other dairy foods, part of the drug may bind with calcium and may not be absorbed properly. This can reduce how well the antibiotic works.
advice_template: If your prescribed antibiotic is affected by dairy, take it 2 to 4 hours apart from milk or other dairy products.

explanation_template: Milk contains calcium, and calcium can interfere with the absorption of certain antibiotics. If milk is taken too close to the medicine, the body may absorb less of the antibiotic than expected. This can make the treatment less effective.
advice_template: Avoid taking milk close to the antibiotic dose unless your healthcare provider says it is safe.

explanation_template: Iron can reduce the absorption of levothyroxine when both are taken too close together. This means the thyroid medicine may not work as well as intended, which can affect thyroid control. Keeping enough time between them helps the medicine absorb properly.
advice_template: Take levothyroxine on an empty stomach and keep iron-containing foods or supplements at least 4 hours apart.

explanation_template: Food can reduce the absorption of levothyroxine if the medicine is taken too close to a meal. As a result, the body may receive less of the medicine than expected, which can reduce its effectiveness. Taking it consistently before الطعام helps improve absorption.
advice_template: Take levothyroxine on an empty stomach, usually 30 minutes before breakfast, unless your doctor has given different instructions.

explanation_template: Leafy green vegetables are rich in vitamin K, and vitamin K can affect how warfarin works in the body. The main issue is not that these foods must always be avoided, but that large changes in intake can change the effect of the medicine. A consistent eating pattern is usually more important than complete avoidance.
advice_template: Do not suddenly increase or decrease leafy green vegetables. Keep your intake consistent and follow INR monitoring advice.

explanation_template: Spinach contains a high amount of vitamin K, which can influence the effect of warfarin. If the amount of spinach eaten changes a lot from day to day, it may affect how well warfarin keeps blood clotting under control. Consistency is important when using this medicine.
advice_template: You do not always need to avoid spinach completely, but keep the amount you eat as consistent as possible.

explanation_template: Alcohol can increase the sedative effect of certain medicines and make you more sleepy, less alert, or dizzy. When alcohol is taken together with a sedating medicine, the effects on the brain can become stronger than expected. This may increase the risk of excessive drowsiness and make daily activities unsafe.
advice_template: Avoid alcohol while taking sedating medicines.

explanation_template: Calcium-containing foods or supplements can reduce the absorption of some antibiotics. When calcium is taken too close to the medicine, less of the antibiotic may enter the bloodstream. This can lower the effectiveness of treatment.
advice_template: Take calcium-rich foods, dairy products, or calcium supplements 2 to 4 hours away from the antibiotic if advised.

explanation_template: Soy products may reduce the absorption of levothyroxine in some people when taken close to the medicine. This can make thyroid treatment less consistent and may affect symptom control. Taking the medicine separately helps improve absorption.
advice_template: Avoid taking soy foods very close to levothyroxine, and follow a consistent routine each day.

explanation_template: A high-carbohydrate meal can raise blood glucose levels and may reduce how well antidiabetic medicines control blood sugar. This does not always mean the medicine fails, but it can make glucose control less stable. Meal size and carbohydrate content are important when using diabetes medicines.
advice_template: Prefer balanced meals, monitor blood sugar when needed, and follow the meal plan recommended for your diabetes treatment.

explanation_template: Taking certain painkillers on an empty stomach can irritate the stomach lining and may lead to stomach pain, burning, or discomfort. Some NSAIDs are better tolerated when taken with food because food helps reduce direct irritation to the stomach.
advice_template: If your medicine instructions allow it, take the painkiller with food or after a meal.

explanation_template: Skipping meals while taking antidiabetic medicine can increase the risk of low blood sugar. When the medicine lowers glucose levels but the body has not received enough food, blood sugar may drop too low and cause symptoms such as dizziness, weakness, shakiness, or sweating. This can happen even if the medicine is taken correctly.
advice_template: Do not skip meals while taking diabetes medicine, and try to eat at regular times each day.

explanation_template: Some antibiotics can cause nausea or stomach discomfort, and the timing of the dose may affect how strongly these symptoms are felt. This does not always mean there is a serious interaction, but it may mean the medicine is irritating the stomach or was taken under less suitable conditions.
advice_template: Follow the instructions given for that antibiotic, and seek advice if nausea continues or becomes severe.

explanation_template: Food may reduce the absorption of iron supplements when they are taken together. This means the body may absorb less iron than expected, although some people tolerate iron better with food. The best timing depends on both absorption and side effects.
advice_template: If your stomach tolerates it, iron is often better absorbed on an empty stomach. Follow your prescribed instructions.

explanation_template: Some vitamins are absorbed better when taken with food, especially when food helps digestion or improves uptake of fat-soluble nutrients. Taking them with a meal may support better absorption and reduce stomach upset in some people.
advice_template: Take the vitamin with food if your instructions recommend it.

explanation_template: Food can change how quickly some antibiotics are absorbed. In some cases this has little effect, while in others it may reduce absorption or delay the medicine’s action. The correct timing depends on the specific antibiotic.
advice_template: Follow the timing instructions given for your prescribed antibiotic.

explanation_template: Food can reduce the absorption of thyroid medication when the dose is taken too close to a meal. This may lower the amount of medicine absorbed and make treatment less consistent. Taking it the same way each day helps keep thyroid control stable.
advice_template: Take thyroid medicine before meals as instructed, usually on an empty stomach.

explanation_template: Dizziness can occur if diabetes medicine is taken without eating enough food. When the medicine lowers blood sugar but the body has not received an adequate meal, the glucose level may drop too low and cause symptoms such as dizziness, weakness, shakiness, or sweating. This is more likely when meals are skipped or delayed.
advice_template: Try to eat regular meals while taking diabetes medicine, and do not skip or delay meals unless your doctor has advised you to do so.

explanation_template: Caffeine can increase alertness and may worsen anxiety symptoms such as nervousness, restlessness, a fast heartbeat, or difficulty sleeping. In some people, this can make it harder to feel the full benefit of anxiety treatment. Sensitivity to caffeine varies from person to person.
advice_template: Limit coffee and other caffeinated drinks if they make anxiety symptoms worse.

explanation_template: Alcohol can strengthen the effect of sedative medicines and make drowsiness more severe. When alcohol is consumed after taking a sedative, it may further slow brain activity, reduce alertness, and make the person feel unusually sleepy or less able to function safely. This combination can increase the risk of excessive sedation and should be avoided.
advice_template: Do not drink alcohol while using sedative medicines.

explanation_template: High sugar intake can raise blood glucose levels and make diabetes harder to control. Even if medicine is being taken correctly, frequent sugary foods or drinks may reduce overall glucose stability. Long-term poor control can increase the risk of complications.
advice_template: Limit sugary foods and drinks, and follow the diet plan recommended for diabetes management.

explanation_template: Eating too much salt can raise blood pressure and reduce how well hypertension treatment works. This may place extra strain on the heart and blood vessels, especially over time. Lowering sodium intake can support better blood pressure control.
advice_template: Reduce salt intake and be careful with processed or packaged foods that contain high sodium.

explanation_template: Grapefruit can affect the way certain statins are broken down in the body. As a result, the medicine level may become higher than expected, which can increase the chance of side effects. The degree of this interaction depends on the specific statin being used.
advice_template: Avoid grapefruit or grapefruit juice unless your prescriber confirms that your statin is safe with it.

explanation_template: Alcohol can worsen the side effects of some antidepressants and may increase drowsiness, dizziness, poor concentration, or emotional instability. In some cases, it may also interfere with recovery and make symptoms harder to manage. Combining alcohol with antidepressants is generally not recommended.
advice_template: Avoid alcohol while taking antidepressants unless your prescriber has clearly advised otherwise.

explanation_template: Smoking can irritate the airways, worsen asthma symptoms, and reduce how well asthma treatment works. It may lead to more frequent coughing, wheezing, shortness of breath, or flare-ups over time. Continuing to smoke can make asthma harder to control.
advice_template: Avoid smoking and reduce exposure to smoke whenever possible.

explanation_template: Nausea may happen when an antibiotic is taken close to dairy foods, because dairy can sometimes affect how the medicine is absorbed or tolerated. This does not always mean there is a serious reaction, but the combination may make stomach discomfort more noticeable in some people. If nausea continues, the timing of food and medicine may need to be adjusted.
advice_template: Try taking dairy foods and the antibiotic a few hours apart if advised, and seek medical advice if nausea continues or becomes worse.

explanation_template: Stomach pain can occur when an NSAID is taken after skipping a meal, because this type of medicine may irritate the stomach lining more when the stomach is empty. Taking the medicine without food can make discomfort, burning, or pain more likely. This is a common timing-related problem with some painkillers.
advice_template: If your medicine instructions allow it, take the painkiller with food or after a meal to reduce stomach irritation.

explanation_template: Dizziness may be caused by low blood sugar if an antidiabetic medicine is taken after skipping a meal. When the medicine lowers blood glucose but enough food is not eaten, the sugar level may drop too much and cause symptoms such as dizziness, weakness, shakiness, or sweating. This can happen even when the medicine is taken correctly.
advice_template: Avoid skipping meals while taking diabetes medicine, and check your blood sugar or seek advice if symptoms continue.

explanation_template: Drowsiness may become worse when alcohol is consumed after taking a sedative medicine. Alcohol can increase the medicine’s calming effect on the brain, leading to stronger sleepiness, reduced alertness, and difficulty doing normal activities safely. This combination can increase the risk of excessive sedation.
advice_template: Do not drink alcohol while using sedative medicines.

explanation_template: Leafy green vegetables contain vitamin K, which can affect how warfarin works in the body. If the amount of these foods you eat changes significantly from day to day, it can alter your blood clotting levels and make the medicine less stable. Sudden increases or decreases in vitamin K intake may reduce the effectiveness or safety of your treatment.
advice_template: Do not suddenly change how much leafy green vegetables you eat. Try to keep your intake consistent and follow your regular monitoring plan.

explanation_template: Alcohol can interact with many medicines in different ways, including increasing drowsiness, irritating the stomach, or affecting how some drugs are processed by the body. The exact risk depends on the medicine, but alcohol often increases the chance of unwanted effects.
advice_template: Limit or avoid alcohol while taking medicine, especially if the medicine can cause sleepiness, stomach upset, or liver-related effects.

explanation_template: A high-fat meal may slow the absorption of some medicines and delay how quickly they start working. In some situations this is not a major problem, but for certain medicines it can change the expected timing or strength of effect.
advice_template: Avoid very heavy or high-fat meals near medicine time if your instructions recommend it.

explanation_template: High-fiber foods can slow the absorption of some medicines when taken at the same time. This may delay the medicine’s effect or reduce how much is absorbed in certain cases. The level of concern depends on the specific medicine.
advice_template: If advised, take high-fiber meals and the medicine at different times.

explanation_template: Missing doses can reduce how well a treatment works and may make the underlying condition harder to control. The impact depends on the type of medicine, but repeated missed doses can reduce the benefit of therapy.
advice_template: Take the medicine exactly as prescribed, and follow the missed-dose instructions given for that specific medicine.

explanation_template: Taking more than the prescribed dose can increase the risk of side effects and, in some cases, may be harmful. The severity depends on the medicine and the amount taken, but double dosing should always be treated seriously.
advice_template: Do not take extra doses. If you think you have taken too much medicine, seek medical advice immediately.
